dimensions.assessment: Affects all minors under 16 using covered platforms across the United States, as well as platform operators and state attorneys general.
dimensions.evidence: A covered platform may not allow an individual to create or maintain an account or profile on the covered platform if the covered platform knows that the individual is a minor.

dimensions.assessment: Resulting actions require termination of existing user accounts and immediate deletion of personal data collected from minors.
dimensions.evidence: terminate the account or profile of the user... immediately delete all personal data collected from the user

dimensions.assessment: Does not authorize direct federal appropriations, though state and federal regulatory enforcement actions involve administrative costs.
Imposes a nationwide statutory ban on minor accounts on covered platforms, preempts state laws on the subject, and grants enforcement powers to the FTC and state attorneys general.
dimensions.evidence: No State or political subdivision of a State may prescribe, maintain, or enforce any law... that relates to the provisions of this section.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent nationwide prohibition taking effect one year after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: this section shall take effect on the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment of this section.

label: H.R. 6488

latest_action.text: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee (Amended) by Voice Vote.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Reducing Exploitative Social Media Exposure for Teens Act (RESET Act) prohibits certain online platforms from allowing minors under the age of 16 to create or maintain an account or profile if the platform knows the user is a minor. It sets timelines for identifying, notifying, and terminating existing minor accounts, requires platforms to delete associated personal data while giving users a limited time to request a copy of their data, and establishes federal and state enforcement mechanisms.

affected_groups.effect: Will be prohibited from creating or maintaining accounts on covered platforms, and existing accounts will be terminated and personal data deleted.
Must prohibit minor accounts, identify and terminate existing minor accounts within specified timelines, delete personal data, and fulfill data access requests.
Given the authority to enforce the rules and penalize violators using the powers of the Federal Trade Commission Act.
Empowered to bring civil actions in state or federal court on behalf of residents to enforce compliance or seek damages, subject to coordination with the Commission.
affected_groups.group: State Attorneys General and state officials

key_provisions: A covered platform may not allow any individual to create or maintain an account or profile if the platform knows the individual is a minor (under age 16).
Existing minor accounts must be identified within 60 days of enactment, users notified within 180 days, and accounts terminated within 30 days of notification.
Platforms must immediately delete personal data of a minor upon account termination, but must allow the user to request a portable and readable copy of their data within 90 days after termination.
Violations of this law are treated as violations of Federal Trade Commission regulations regarding unfair or deceptive acts or practices, enforceable by the Commission.

State attorneys general or other state officials may bring civil actions on behalf of state residents to enforce compliance, obtain damages, or enjoin violations, subject to Federal Trade Commission notice and intervention rules.
State-level laws relating to the provisions of this section are preempted, meaning no state may enforce its own rules on this specific matter.
missing_information: The definition or specific criteria for what constitutes a 'covered platform', as it relies on an external reference to the TAKE IT DOWN Act.
The exact monetary penalties for violations, as they depend on the incorporated provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act rather than being explicitly written in the text.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Reducing Exploitative Social Media Exposure for Teens Act (RESET Act) prohibits certain online platforms from allowing minors under the age of 16 to create or maintain an account or profile if the platform knows the user is a minor. It sets timelines for identifying, notifying, and terminating existing minor accounts, requires platforms to delete associated personal data while giving users a limited time to request a copy of their data, and establishes federal and state enforcement mechanisms.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a nationwide ban on minors under 16 having accounts or profiles on covered social platforms, preempting state laws, creating strict data deletion requirements, and establishing federal and state enforcement mechanisms.
